# 2 Samuel 4 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 4 (12 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 7

---

## V.1 — "courage failed" vs. "dropped his hands" vs. "lost all nerve"
- **EMET:** "dropped his-hands" / **LOGOS:** "his courage failed him" / **PNEUMA:** "lost all nerve"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his courage failed him" — idiom accurately rendered.

---

## V.4 — "crippled in feet" vs. "lame in both feet"
- **EMET:** "smitten of-feet" / **LOGOS:** "crippled in his feet" / **PNEUMA:** "lame in both feet"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "crippled in his feet" — "both" not in Hebrew.

---

## V.4 — Nurse scene: "he fell" vs. "she dropped him"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "he fell and became lame"
- **PNEUMA:** "she dropped him, and he was crippled"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "he fell and became lame" — PNEUMA adds interpretation beyond the text.

---

## V.6 — Entry pretext rendering
- **EMET:** "taking wheat" / **LOGOS:** "as though fetching wheat" / **PNEUMA:** "slipped inside as if collecting wheat"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "as though fetching wheat" — formal register with ruse sense.

---

## V.8 — "gave vengeance" vs. "has avenged"
- **EMET:** "gave...vengeance" / **LOGOS:** "has avenged" / **PNEUMA:** "has given...vengeance"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "has avenged" — natural English for the theological claim.

---

## V.10 — "good news" vs. "wonderful news"
- **LOGOS:** "good news" / **PNEUMA:** "wonderful news"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "good news" — "wonderful" over-translates *besorah*.

---

## V.11 — "righteous" vs. "innocent"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "righteous" / **PNEUMA:** "innocent"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "righteous" — *tsaddiq* is stronger than mere innocence.

---
*— SOPHIA*
